question: A 3-year-old male is brought to the ER with a sore throat and fever. Examination of the pharynx reveals a dark, inflammatory exudate. Cysteine-tellurite agar culture produces black, iridescent colonies. Microscopic features of the causal organism most likely include which of the following?
analysis: The clinical presentation of a sore throat, fever, and dark inflammatory exudate, along with the culture results showing black, iridescent colonies on cysteine-tellurite agar, is indicative of diphtheria caused by Corynebacterium diphtheriae. This organism is known for its characteristic metachromic granules, which can be observed under the microscope. Therefore, the most likely microscopic feature of the causal organism is the presence of metachromic granules.
